purpose: Reslizumab is used to help control severe asthma in adults whose asthma is linked to high levels of certain white blood cells called eosinophils. It is used as an add-on treatment, meaning it works alongside your other asthma medicines. It helps reduce how often you have asthma attacks and makes it easier to breathe day to day.
how_it_works: Your body makes a protein called interleukin-5 (IL-5) that tells certain allergy-related white blood cells, called eosinophils, to grow and cause swelling in your airways. Reslizumab is like a targeted blocker that attaches to IL-5 and stops it from working. With fewer eosinophils active in your lungs, there is less inflammation and your airways stay more open.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a sore throat, muscle pain or weakness, and a small increase in a certain enzyme in the blood called creatine phosphokinase. Some people may also feel tired or have mild reactions during or after the infusion.
warnings: A serious allergic reaction called anaphylaxis can happen during or shortly after the infusion, so you will always be watched by a healthcare provider during treatment. If you develop hives, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, or trouble breathing, tell someone right away. Do not use this medicine to treat a sudden asthma attack — it will not work fast enough in an emergency. Also let your doctor know if you have a parasitic infection before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: Reslizumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion into a vein, typically once every 4 weeks. The dose is based on your body weight (3 mg per kilogram). Each infusion usually takes about 20 to 50 minutes and is always given by a healthcare provider in a clinical setting.
